name:
Fraksi PPP
(Hamzah Haz)
summary:
Chaired by the measured budget veteran Hamzah Haz, the United Development Party (PPP) stands as the oldest surviving Islamic party in the Republic. Born out of Suharto's forced 1973 merger of four Muslim parties, the Ka'bah party defied predictions that new rivals like PKB and PAN would hollow out its base, capturing 10.71% of the national ballot—11.3 million votes and fifty-eight parliamentary seats—to finish third in June 1999. That resilience rests on a quarter-century of parish-level organizing across Aceh, West Java, South Kalimantan, West Sumatra, and Madura, where loyal ulama and rural boarding schools (pesantren) rallied to the restored Ka'bah banner.

Though Hamzah Haz served a full year inside your cabinet as State Minister of Investment (BKPM) before stepping down in May 1999 to lead PPP's campaign, thirty years of surviving New Order parliaments have trained him never to lash his party to a sinking hull. PPP's clerical council rejects secularization and invokes classical fiqh doctrine to oppose a female president, erecting an ideological wall between Hamzah Haz and Megawati Sukarnoputri. Yet Hamzah knows every skeleton in your administration's closet and keeps his caucus positioned to pivot toward Amien Rais's Central Axis if your numbers falter. Preserving public order across the provinces and commanding broad popular approval give the Palace strong leverage over PPP's cautious lawmakers, who dread street upheaval and shrink from backing an isolated president.
biography:
Born in Ketapang, West Kalimantan, on February 15, 1940, Hamzah Haz taught school, edited a Pontianak newspaper, and chaired rural banking cooperatives before entering the West Kalimantan provincial legislature in 1968 under the banner of Nahdlatul Ulama. Moving to Senayan in 1971, he absorbed the shock of January 5, 1973, when the New Order forced NU, Parmusi, PSII, and PERTI to fuse into PPP. Over the next quarter-century—even after NU withdrew from formal party politics in 1984 and Suharto's Asas Tunggal laws stripped PPP of its Islamic foundation and Ka'bah emblem—Hamzah stayed inside parliament, mastering the state ledger on the DPR Budget Commission (Komisi APBN).

You brought him into the Development Reform Cabinet as Minister of Investment in May 1998. Six months later, at PPP's Fourth National Congress (Muktamar IV) at Pondok Gede, delegates restored Islam as the party's ideological foundation, brought back the Ka'bah symbol, and elected Hamzah Haz party chairman over A.M. Saefuddin. When Golkar demanded that ministers from rival parties resign ahead of the June 1999 campaign, Hamzah surrendered his portfolio without rancor and steered PPP to fifty-eight seats. An understated accountant by training and temperament, he weighs your accountability report like a balance sheet—ready to extend credit if your government stays solvent, or call in his markers with Amien Rais and Gus Dur if the Palace faces bankruptcy.

interactions.text: Ring-fence Ministry of Religious Affairs madrasah subsidies against IMF austerity cuts
interactions.description: Structural adjustment targets drafted by the IMF call for across-the-board reductions in social spending, threatening the Ministry of Religious Affairs (Depag) grant lines that sustain the Madrasah Diniyah and rural pesantren networks anchoring PPP's electorate. Give Hamzah Haz and parliamentary whip Zarkasih Nur a written guarantee that religious schooling funds remain untouched. Secures a binding political debt from PPP's leadership that carries forward into the Central Axis.
interactions.alertMsg: As a veteran of the DPR Budget Commission, Hamzah Haz inspects the revised Depag budget tables himself before nodding in approval. With their rural madrasah funding protected from the IMF's scalpel, PPP's lawmakers warm toward Bina Graha.

interactions.text: Pledge the Coordinating Ministry for Economy and Finance (Menko Ekuin) to Hamzah Haz
interactions.description: Hamzah Haz spent a year running the Investment Coordinating Board (BKPM) in your cabinet before Golkar forced party chairmen to vacate their ministerial posts in May 1999. Promise him that if your administration wins a full mandate in October, he will return to the cabinet room promoted to Coordinating Minister for Economy, Finance, and Industry (Menko Ekuin). Binds PPP's leadership with a lasting political obligation that carries forward into the Central Axis.
interactions.alertMsg: Hamzah Haz receives the offer with his trademark understated composure. Having spent decades mastering state budgets from the opposition benches, the prospect of helming Indonesia's entire economic cabinet softens his caucus's posture toward the Palace.

interactions.text: Amplify the clerical fiqh debate over female executive leadership
interactions.description: Since the November 1998 Congress of the Indonesian Muslim Community (KUII) and fiery statements by PPP minister A.M. Saefuddin, conservative ulama inside PPP's Majelis Syariah have argued that Islamic jurisprudence forbids a woman from serving as head of state—a ruling aimed straight at Megawati Sukarnoputri. Use state-linked Islamic publications and Friday pulpit networks to give those clerical rulings wider circulation.
interactions.alertMsg: Tracts and Friday sermons debating female leadership multiply across West Java, Madura, and South Kalimantan, hardening the theological barrier between PPP's fifty-eight delegates and Megawati's camp while provoking outrage from PDI Perjuangan and civil-society feminists.

interactions.text: Pay a state visit to PPP's flagship pesantren strongholds in Madura and Rembang
interactions.description: Even after Gus Dur launched PKB, revered traditionalist kiai like K.H. Alawy Muhammad in Sampang, Madura, and K.H. Maimun Zubair at Pesantren Al-Anwar in Sarang, Rembang, kept their flocks loyal to the Ka'bah. Travel by presidential helicopter to pay homage at their boarding schools,wearing a peci and joining the santri in afternoon prayer.
interactions.alertMsg: Photographs of you kneeling beside the senior kiai of Madura and Rembang run across the front pages of the Islamic press. The elders of PPP's Majelis Syariah send warm word to Hamzah Haz in Jakarta.

interactions.text: Repudiate the New Order's 1973 forced party fusion and Asas Tunggal coercion on the record
interactions.description: For veterans of PPP like Hamzah Haz, Bachtiar Chamsyah, and Aisyah Aminy, the trauma of Suharto's 1973 party fusion—followed by intelligence operative Ali Moertopo's meddling and the 1984 law that outlawed the Ka'bah emblem—remains a bitter memory. Deliver a formal speech acknowledging that the New Order's subjugation of PPP was an abuse of state power.
interactions.alertMsg: Veteran Ka'bah lawmakers who endured decades of state surveillance and forced leadership coups under the New Order greet your statement with visible emotion, while old-guard Golkar operatives bristle at the indictment of Suharto's political architecture.
